records.literal_gloss: and you will say to Tyre, who sits at [the] entrances of [the] sea, the trader of the peoples to many coastlands: Thus says [the] Lord Yahweh: Tyre, you have said, I [am] perfect of beauty.

en.L: and say to Tyre, who dwells at the entrances of the sea, \q the trader of the peoples to many coastlands, \q Thus says the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}}: \q Tyre, you have said, "I [am] perfect in beauty."
en.B: and say to Tyre, the city that sits at the gateways of the sea, \q trading with the peoples of many coastlands, \q The Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says this: \q Tyre, you have said, "I am perfect in beauty."
en.R: Say to Tyre, the city at the harbor gates of the sea, \q which trades with peoples in many lands far away, \q This is what the Lord {{divine_name:GOD|Yahweh}} says: \q Tyre, you have said, "I am perfectly beautiful."

es.R: Dile a Tiro, la ciudad que está en los puertos del mar, \q y que comercia con pueblos de muchas tierras lejanas: \q Esto es lo que dice el Señor {{divine_name:DIOS|Yahvé}}: \q Tiro, tú has dicho: «Soy perfectamente hermosa».

decisions.choice: the lament pictures Tyre as a great merchant ship
decisions.reason: The poem tells the story of a ship: how it was built from the finest materials (verses 4-7), crewed and guarded (8-11), loaded with the trade of the whole known world (12-25), and wrecked at sea, while sailors on the shore mourn it (26-36). Tyre, an island city that lived by the sea, is that ship. The chapter is set in lines as poetry from here to verse 36, following the Hebrew accents. The list of trading partners in verses 12-24 reads like a merchant's register and is set in lines too, so that the poem is not broken.

decisions.choice: the entrances of the sea: harbors
decisions.reason: Tyre had harbors on its island, the gates through which the sea trade came in and went out.

decisions.choice: I am perfect in beauty: the boast the lament answers
decisions.reason: Tyre's own words sum up its pride. The same "perfect in beauty" is said of the king of Tyre (28:12) and of Jerusalem, also brought low (Lamentations 2:15; Ezekiel 16:14).

decisions.choice: no quotation marks for the message; double quotation marks for Tyre's boast
decisions.reason: Under the quotation rule for Ezekiel, the message Ezekiel is told to deliver takes no quotation marks, and human speech quoted inside it takes double quotes. "Coastlands" follows the Isaiah table ("lands far away" at Readable).

decisions.choice: the lament over Tyre (27:3b-36) set in lines; Tyre, pictured as a ship, keeps the feminine ("parfaite", "tu as été remplie") at every level
alternatives: masculine agreement for the ship ("le navire")
decisions.reason: The term sheet names Tyre in Ezekiel 27 as a city addressed as a woman; French keeps the city's agreement even where the picture is a ship.

decisions.choice: the lament in lines; no quotation marks for the message, « » for Tyre's boast; feminine 'tú'
decisions.reason: The lament over Tyre as a ship (3b-36) is set in lines, as the English does. The message Ezekiel delivers takes no marks; Tyre's own boast is human speech and takes « ». The city, and the ship it is pictured as, are feminine (perfecta), as in the Hebrew.

decisions.choice: the lament set in lines, God's message without quotation marks, Tyre's boast in double quotes; Tyre as a ship
decisions.reason: As the English record; Swahili "meli" (ship) is not named in the text, which keeps the Hebrew picture implicit, as the meaning decision explains.

decisions.choice: The lament is set in lines with no quotation marks; Tyre's boast takes double quotes and "ta"
alternatives: quotation marks around the whole lament
decisions.reason: As the English: the message Ezekiel is told to deliver is God's speech and takes no quotation marks (term sheet). Tyre, pictured in the poem as a great ship, is still addressed as "ngươi".

records.literal_gloss: In [the] heart of [the] seas [are] your borders; your builders perfected your beauty.

en.L: In the heart of the seas [are] your borders; \q your builders made your beauty perfect.
en.B: Your territory is in the heart of the seas; \q your builders made your beauty perfect.
en.R: Your home is far out in the sea. \q Those who built you made you perfectly beautiful.

fr.L: Au cœur des mers [sont] tes frontières ; \q tes bâtisseurs ont rendu parfaite ta beauté.
fr.B: Ton domaine est au cœur des mers ; \q tes bâtisseurs ont rendu ta beauté parfaite.

decisions.choice: the heart of the seas: the open sea
decisions.reason: The phrase means the high seas, far from shore (verses 25-27). It fits both the ship and the island city.

decisions.choice: your builders: the picture becomes a ship
decisions.reason: From here the city is described as a ship that its builders made perfect.

source.text: בְּרוֹשִׁ֤ים מִשְּׂנִיר֙ בָּ֣נוּ לָ֔ךְ אֵ֖ת כָּל־לֻֽחֹתָ֑יִם אֶ֤רֶז מִלְּבָנוֹן֙ לָקָ֔חוּ לַעֲשׂ֥וֹת תֹּ֖רֶן עָלָֽיִךְ׃

fr.R: Tes constructeurs ont utilisé les genévriers du mont Hermon pour faire toutes tes planches. \q Ils ont pris un cèdre du Liban pour faire ton mât.

es.L: De cipreses de Senir te construyeron todas las tablas; \q un cedro del Líbano tomaron para hacerte un mástil.
es.B: Construyeron todas tus tablas con cipreses de Senir; \q tomaron un cedro del Líbano para hacer tu mástil.
es.R: Tus constructores usaron cipreses del monte Hermón para hacer todas tus tablas. \q Tomaron un cedro del Líbano para hacer tu mástil.

sw.L: Kwa mireteni kutoka Seniri walikujengea mbao zako zote; \q walichukua mwerezi kutoka Lebanoni ili kukutengenezea mlingoti.
sw.B: Walizitengeneza mbao zako zote kwa mireteni ya Seniri; \q mwerezi kutoka Lebanoni ulichukuliwa kuwa mlingoti wako.
sw.R: Wajenzi wako walitumia mireteni ya mlima Hermoni kutengeneza mbao zako zote. \q Walichukua mwerezi kutoka Lebanoni kutengeneza mlingoti wako.

vi.L: Bằng gỗ bách xù từ Sê-nia, chúng đã đóng mọi tấm ván cho ngươi; \q chúng đã lấy một cây bá hương từ Li-ban để làm cột buồm cho ngươi.
vi.B: Họ đóng mọi tấm ván của ngươi bằng gỗ bách xù từ Sê-nia; \q họ lấy một cây bá hương từ Li-ban làm cột buồm cho ngươi.
vi.R: Những người đóng ngươi đã dùng cây bách xù từ núi Hẹt-môn để làm mọi tấm ván của ngươi. \q Họ lấy một cây bá hương từ Li-ban để làm cột buồm cho ngươi.

decisions.choice: Senir: Mount Hermon
decisions.reason: Senir was the Amorite name of Mount Hermon, north of Israel (Deuteronomy 3:9).

decisions.choice: junipers and a cedar from Lebanon: the finest timber of the region
decisions.reason: The tall conifers of the Lebanon and Hermon ranges were prized for building (1 Kings 5:20-24). A straight cedar made a fine mast.

decisions.choice: Mount Hermon
decisions.reason: Readable gives the familiar name of the mountain. "Junipers" follows Isaiah 14:8.

decisions.choice: cipreses de Senir (L, B); cipreses del monte Hermón (R)
decisions.reason: The tree (berosh) is worded as in Spanish Kings ('ciprés'); Senir keeps its published name, and R gives the mountain's better-known name, as the English R does.

decisions.choice: "mireteni" for the junipers; "Seniri" (L, B), "mlima Hermoni" (R)
decisions.reason: "mreteni" as the Swahili Isaiah 41:19 and 60:13; "Seniri" as 1 Chronicles 5:23.

decisions.choice: "gỗ bách xù" for the junipers; "Sê-nia" (L, B) / "núi Hẹt-môn" (R); the builders are "họ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: "Sê-nia" is the published form (Deuteronomy 3:9). The shipbuilders are neutral, not under judgment, so B and R call them "họ"; L keeps the plain "chúng" of the Hebrew's "they".

source.text: אַלּוֹנִים֙ מִבָּ֔שָׁן עָשׂ֖וּ מִשּׁוֹטָ֑יִךְ קַרְשֵׁ֤ךְ עָֽשׂוּ־שֵׁן֙ בַּת־אֲשֻׁרִ֔ים מֵאִיֵּ֖י כִּתִּיִּֽים׃

records.literal_gloss: [Of] oaks from Bashan they made your oars; your deck they made [of] ivory, daughter of Ashurim, from [the] coastlands of Kittim.

en.L: [Of] oaks from Bashan they made your oars; \q your deck they made of ivory [set in] box wood from the coastlands of Kittim.
en.B: They made your oars of oaks from Bashan; \q they made your deck of box wood from the coastlands of Kittim, inlaid with ivory.
en.R: Your oars were made of oak trees from Bashan. \q Your deck was made of box wood from Cyprus and decorated with ivory.

fr.L: [En] chênes du Bashân ils ont fait tes rames ; \q ton pont, ils l’ont fait d’ivoire [serti dans] du buis des îles de Kittim.
fr.B: Ils ont fait tes rames avec les chênes du Bashân ; \q ils ont fait ton pont de buis des îles de Kittim, incrusté d’ivoire.
fr.R: Tes rames étaient faites de chênes du Bashân. \q Ton pont était fait de buis de Chypre et décoré d’ivoire.

es.L: De encinas de Basán hicieron tus remos; \q tu cubierta hicieron de marfil [engastado en] boj de las costas de Quitim.
es.B: Hicieron tus remos con encinas de Basán; \q hicieron tu cubierta con boj de las costas de Quitim, con incrustaciones de marfil.
es.R: Tus remos los hicieron con encinas de Basán. \q Tu cubierta la hicieron con boj de Chipre y la decoraron con marfil.

sw.L: [Kwa] mialoni ya Bashani walitengeneza makasia yako; \q sitaha yako waliifanya kwa pembe za ndovu [zilizopachikwa] katika mberoshi kutoka visiwa vya Kitimu.
sw.B: Walitengeneza makasia yako kwa mialoni ya Bashani; \q waliifanya sitaha yako kwa mberoshi kutoka pwani za Kitimu, iliyopambwa kwa pembe za ndovu.
sw.R: Makasia yako yalitengenezwa kwa mialoni ya Bashani. \q Sitaha yako ilitengenezwa kwa mbao za mberoshi kutoka Kipro, ikapambwa kwa pembe za ndovu.

vi.L: [Bằng] gỗ sồi từ Ba-san, chúng đã làm mái chèo của ngươi; \q sàn tàu của ngươi, chúng đã làm bằng ngà [cẩn trên] gỗ hoàng dương từ các hải đảo Kít-tim.
vi.B: Họ làm mái chèo của ngươi bằng gỗ sồi Ba-san; \q họ làm sàn tàu ngươi bằng gỗ hoàng dương từ các hải đảo Kít-tim, có cẩn ngà.
vi.R: Mái chèo của ngươi được làm bằng gỗ sồi Ba-san. \q Sàn tàu của ngươi được làm bằng gỗ hoàng dương từ đảo Chíp-rơ và trang trí bằng ngà voi.

decisions.choice: oaks from Bashan: the famous oaks east of the Sea of Galilee
decisions.reason: Bashan was known for its oaks and its cattle (Isaiah 2:13; Amos 4:1).

decisions.choice: ivory set in box wood
alternatives: ivory, the work of the Ashurites
decisions.reason: Divided as the Hebrew text has it, the words read "ivory, daughter of the Ashurites". Read as one word, they give the name of a tree, the box tree (Isaiah 41:19; 60:13), and the sense "ivory in box wood". The second reading is followed here.

decisions.choice: Kittim: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Kittim is named after the city of Kition on Cyprus and stands for Cyprus and the islands west of it (Isaiah 23:1, 12).

decisions.choice: Cyprus
decisions.reason: Readable says "Cyprus" for Kittim, as the Isaiah table sets.

decisions.choice: "les îles de Kittim" (L, B); "Chypre" (R)
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names table: Kittim (L, B) / Chypre (R), as the English R says Cyprus.

decisions.choice: Quitim (L, B); Chipre (R)
decisions.reason: Kittim is worded as in Spanish Isaiah at each level.

decisions.choice: "mberoshi" for the box tree; "Kitimu" (L, B), "Kipro" (R)
decisions.reason: "mberoshi" as the Swahili Isaiah 60:13; Kittim as the Swahili Isaiah has it, with Readable naming Cyprus as the English Readable does.

source.text: שֵׁשׁ־בְּרִקְמָ֤ה מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ הָיָ֣ה מִפְרָשֵׂ֔ךְ לִהְי֥וֹת לָ֖ךְ לְנֵ֑ס תְּכֵ֧לֶת וְאַרְגָּמָ֛ן מֵאִיֵּ֥י אֱלִישָׁ֖ה הָיָ֥ה מְכַסֵּֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Fine linen with embroidery from Egypt was your sail, to be for you a banner; blue and purple from [the] coastlands of Elishah was your covering.

en.L: Fine linen with embroidered work from Egypt was your sail, \q to be your banner; \q blue and purple from the coastlands of Elishah was your awning.
en.B: Your sail was of fine embroidered linen from Egypt, \q and it served as your banner; \q your awning was of blue and purple cloth from the coastlands of Elishah.
en.R: Your sail was made of fine linen from Egypt, with colorful designs. \q It was your flag. \q Your sunshade was made of blue and purple cloth from the coasts of Elishah.

fr.L: Le fin lin brodé d’Égypte était ta voile, \q pour te servir d’étendard ; \q le bleu et la pourpre des îles d’Élisha étaient ton abri.
fr.B: Ta voile était de fin lin brodé d’Égypte, \q et elle te servait d’étendard ; \q ton abri était d’étoffes bleues et pourpres des îles d’Élisha.
fr.R: Ta voile était faite de fin lin d’Égypte, avec des dessins de couleur. \q C’était ton drapeau. \q Ton toit contre le soleil était fait de tissu bleu et pourpre venu des côtes d’Élisha.

es.L: Lino fino con bordados de Egipto era tu vela, \q para que te sirviera de estandarte; \q azul y púrpura de las costas de Elisa era tu toldo.
es.B: Tu vela era de lino fino bordado de Egipto, \q y te servía de estandarte; \q tu toldo era de tela azul y púrpura de las costas de Elisa.
es.R: Tu vela estaba hecha de lino fino de Egipto, con dibujos de colores. \q Era tu bandera. \q Tu toldo para el sol estaba hecho de tela azul y púrpura de las costas de Elisa.

sw.L: Kitani safi chenye kazi ya kutariziwa kutoka Misri kilikuwa tanga lako, \q ili kiwe bendera yako; \q samawati na zambarau kutoka visiwa vya Elisha vilikuwa kifuniko chako.
sw.B: Tanga lako lilikuwa la kitani safi kilichotariziwa kutoka Misri, \q nalo lilikuwa bendera yako; \q kifuniko chako kilikuwa cha nguo ya samawati na zambarau kutoka pwani za Elisha.
sw.R: Tanga lako lilitengenezwa kwa kitani safi cha Misri, chenye michoro ya rangi. \q Lilikuwa bendera yako. \q Kivuli chako cha kukukinga na jua kilitengenezwa kwa nguo ya samawati na zambarau kutoka pwani za Elisha.

vi.L: Vải gai mịn có thêu từ Ai Cập là cánh buồm của ngươi, \q để làm cờ hiệu cho ngươi; \q vải xanh và tím từ các hải đảo Ê-li-sa là mái che của ngươi.
vi.B: Cánh buồm của ngươi bằng vải gai mịn có thêu từ Ai Cập, \q dùng làm cờ hiệu của ngươi; \q mái che của ngươi bằng vải xanh và tím từ các hải đảo Ê-li-sa.
vi.R: Cánh buồm của ngươi làm bằng vải gai mịn từ Ai Cập, có thêu hoa văn nhiều màu. \q Đó là lá cờ của ngươi. \q Tấm che nắng của ngươi làm bằng vải xanh và tím từ miền duyên hải Ê-li-sa.

decisions.choice: fine linen with embroidery from Egypt
decisions.reason: Egypt was famous for its fine linen (Proverbs 7:16). Such a sail was a luxury.

decisions.choice: a banner: the sail served as the ship's emblem
decisions.reason: The word means a flag or signal. The splendid sail marked the ship from afar.

decisions.choice: blue and purple from Elishah
decisions.reason: Blue and purple dyes were costly; purple was the great product of Phoenicia itself. Elishah is a son of Javan in Genesis 10:4 and probably a land in the west, perhaps on Cyprus.

decisions.choice: sunshade (R); awning (L, B)
decisions.reason: The covering was an awning over the deck. Readable says what it was for.

source.text: יֹשְׁבֵ֤י צִידוֹן֙ וְאַרְוַ֔ד הָי֥וּ שָׁטִ֖ים לָ֑ךְ חֲכָמַ֤יִךְ צוֹר֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה חֹבְלָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were rowers for you; your skilled [men], Tyre, were in you; they [were] your sailors.

en.L: The inhabitants of Sidon and Arvad were rowers for you; \q your skilled men, Tyre, were in you; they [were] your sailors.
en.B: Men from Sidon and Arvad were your rowers; \q your own skilled men, Tyre, were on board as your sailors.
en.R: Men from the cities of Sidon and Arvad rowed for you. \q Your own skilled men, Tyre, were the sailors who steered you.

fr.L: Les habitants de Sidon et d’Arvad étaient tes rameurs ; \q tes sages, Tyr, étaient en toi ; eux, [ils étaient] tes matelots.
fr.B: Les hommes de Sidon et d’Arvad étaient tes rameurs ; \q tes propres experts, Tyr, étaient à bord comme matelots.
fr.R: Des hommes des villes de Sidon et d’Arvad ramaient pour toi. \q Tes propres hommes habiles, Tyr, étaient les marins qui te dirigeaient.

es.L: Los habitantes de Sidón y de Arvad eran tus remeros; \q tus sabios, Tiro, estaban en ti; ellos [eran] tus marineros.
es.B: Hombres de Sidón y de Arvad eran tus remeros; \q tus propios hombres expertos, Tiro, iban a bordo como tus marineros.
es.R: Hombres de las ciudades de Sidón y de Arvad remaban para ti. \q Tus propios hombres expertos, Tiro, eran los marineros que te guiaban.

sw.L: Wakaaji wa Sidoni na Arvadi walikuwa wapiga makasia wako; \q watu wako stadi, Tiro, walikuwa ndani yako; wao [walikuwa] mabaharia wako.
sw.B: Watu wa Sidoni na Arvadi walikuwa wapiga makasia wako; \q watu wako wenyewe wenye ujuzi, Tiro, walikuwa melini kama mabaharia wako.
sw.R: Watu wa miji ya Sidoni na Arvadi walikupigia makasia. \q Watu wako wenyewe wenye ujuzi, Tiro, ndio walikuwa mabaharia walioongoza safari yako.

vi.L: Dân cư Si-đôn và A-vát là những tay chèo của ngươi; \q những người tài giỏi của ngươi, hỡi Ty-rơ, ở trong ngươi; họ [là] thủy thủ của ngươi.
vi.B: Người Si-đôn và người A-vát là những tay chèo của ngươi; \q chính những người tài giỏi của ngươi, hỡi Ty-rơ, ở trên tàu làm thủy thủ cho ngươi.
vi.R: Những người từ các thành Si-đôn và A-vát chèo thuyền cho ngươi. \q Chính những người tài giỏi của ngươi, hỡi Ty-rơ, là những thủy thủ lái tàu cho ngươi.

decisions.choice: Sidon and Arvad: Phoenician cities north of Tyre
decisions.reason: Sidon, Tyre's older sister city, lay about twenty-five miles to the north (28:21). Arvad was an island city farther north, on the coast of Syria (Genesis 10:18).

decisions.choice: your skilled men were your sailors: Tyre's own men held the skilled posts
decisions.reason: Other cities supplied the rowers; Tyre's own men were the sailors who handled the ship.

decisions.choice: sailors
decisions.reason: The word for the ship's skilled hands (those who handle the ropes) is "sailors" at every level in this chapter, and the more general word in verses 9, 27 and 29 is "mariners" (L, B) or "seamen" (R).

decisions.choice: "A-vát" for Arvad
decisions.reason: No published form of the city's name; Genesis 10:18 has the people "người A-va-đít", and "A-vát" follows it. The same in verse 11.

source.text: זִקְנֵ֨י גְבַ֤ל וַחֲכָמֶ֨יהָ֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ מַחֲזִיקֵ֖י בִּדְקֵ֑ךְ כָּל־אֳנִיּ֨וֹת הַיָּ֤ם וּמַלָּֽחֵיהֶם֙ הָ֣יוּ בָ֔ךְ לַעֲרֹ֖ב מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] elders of Gebal and its wise [men] were in you, repairing your seams; all [the] ships of the sea and their mariners were in you, to trade your merchandise.

en.L: The elders of Gebal and its wise men were in you, \q repairing your seams; \q all the ships of the sea and their mariners were in you \q to trade your merchandise.
en.B: The veteran craftsmen of Gebal were on board, \q caulking your seams. \q All the ships of the sea and their crews came to you \q to barter for your goods.
en.R: Experienced workers from Gebal were with you. \q They sealed the cracks between your boards. \q All the ships on the sea and their seamen came to you \q to trade for your goods.

fr.L: Les anciens de Guebal et ses sages étaient en toi, \q réparant tes fissures ; \q tous les navires de la mer et leurs marins étaient en toi \q pour échanger tes marchandises.
fr.B: Les artisans chevronnés de Guebal étaient à bord, \q et ils calfataient tes fentes. \q Tous les navires de la mer et leurs équipages venaient chez toi \q pour échanger tes marchandises.
fr.R: Des ouvriers expérimentés de Guebal étaient avec toi. \q Ils bouchaient les fentes entre tes planches. \q Tous les bateaux de la mer et leurs marins venaient chez toi \q pour acheter tes marchandises.

es.L: Los ancianos de Gebal y sus sabios estaban en ti, \q reparando tus junturas; \q todas las naves del mar y sus marinos estaban en ti \q para negociar tus mercancías.
es.B: Los artesanos veteranos de Gebal iban a bordo, \q calafateando tus junturas. \q Todas las naves del mar y sus tripulaciones venían a ti \q para comerciar con tus mercancías.
es.R: Trabajadores con experiencia de Gebal estaban contigo. \q Tapaban las rendijas entre tus tablas. \q Todos los barcos del mar y sus marineros venían a ti \q para comerciar con tus mercancías.

sw.L: Wazee wa Gebali na wenye hekima wake walikuwa ndani yako, \q wakiziba nyufa zako; \q meli zote za bahari na mabaharia wake zilikuwa ndani yako \q ili kufanya biashara ya bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Mafundi wazoefu wa Gebali walikuwa melini, \q wakiziba nyufa zako. \q Meli zote za bahari na mabaharia wake zilikujia \q ili kubadilishana bidhaa zako.
sw.R: Mafundi wenye uzoefu kutoka Gebali walikuwa pamoja nawe. \q Waliziba nyufa kati ya mbao zako. \q Meli zote za baharini na mabaharia wake zilikujia \q ili kununua bidhaa zako.

vi.L: Các trưởng lão của Ghê-banh và những người khôn ngoan của nó ở trong ngươi, \q trám các đường nối của ngươi; \q mọi tàu bè trên biển cùng các thủy thủ của chúng ở trong ngươi \q để trao đổi hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.B: Những thợ lành nghề lão luyện của Ghê-banh ở trên tàu, \q trám các kẽ hở của ngươi. \q Mọi tàu bè trên biển cùng thủy thủ của chúng đều đến với ngươi \q để đổi chác hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Những thợ giàu kinh nghiệm từ Ghê-banh ở với ngươi. \q Họ trám kín các kẽ hở giữa những tấm ván của ngươi. \q Mọi tàu bè trên biển cùng các thủy thủ của chúng đều đến với ngươi \q để mua bán hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: Gebal: the Phoenician city of Byblos
decisions.reason: Gebal, north of modern Beirut, was known for its skilled builders (1 Kings 5:32; Joshua 13:5).

decisions.choice: the elders and wise men of Gebal: master craftsmen
decisions.reason: Here "elders" and "wise men" are experienced, skilled workers.

decisions.choice: all the ships of the sea came to you
decisions.reason: The picture widens from one ship to the harbor city, where the ships of every nation came to trade.

decisions.choice: "Guebal" at every level
decisions.reason: The form of published 1 Kings 5:32 and of the term sheet; the meaning decision names Byblos.

source.text: פָּרַ֨ס וְל֤וּד וּפוּט֙ הָי֣וּ בְחֵילֵ֔ךְ אַנְשֵׁ֖י מִלְחַמְתֵּ֑ךְ מָגֵ֤ן וְכוֹבַע֙ תִּלּוּ־בָ֔ךְ הֵ֖מָּה נָתְנ֥וּ הֲדָרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war; shield and helmet they hung in you; they gave your splendor.

en.L: Persia and Lud and Put were in your army, your men of war; \q shield and helmet they hung in you; \q they gave you your splendor.
en.B: Men of Persia, Lud and Put served in your army as your warriors. \q They hung their shields and helmets in you; \q they gave you your splendor.
en.R: Soldiers from Persia, Lud and Put served in your army. \q They hung up their shields and helmets inside you. \q They made you look splendid.

fr.L: La Perse, Lud et Puth étaient dans ton armée, tes hommes de guerre ; \q le bouclier et le casque, ils les suspendaient chez toi ; \q ils te donnaient ta splendeur.
fr.B: Des hommes de Perse, de Lud et de Puth servaient dans ton armée comme guerriers. \q Ils suspendaient chez toi leurs boucliers et leurs casques ; \q ils te donnaient ta splendeur.
fr.R: Des soldats de Perse, de Lud et de Puth servaient dans ton armée. \q Ils accrochaient leurs boucliers et leurs casques chez toi. \q Grâce à eux, tu étais magnifique.

es.L: Persia y Lud y Fut estaban en tu ejército, tus hombres de guerra; \q escudo y yelmo colgaron en ti; \q ellos te dieron tu esplendor.
es.B: Hombres de Persia, de Lud y de Fut servían en tu ejército como tus guerreros. \q Colgaban en ti sus escudos y sus cascos; \q ellos te daban tu esplendor.
es.R: Soldados de Persia, de Lud y de Fut servían en tu ejército. \q Colgaban sus escudos y sus cascos dentro de ti. \q Te hacían lucir espléndida.

sw.L: Uajemi na Ludi na Puti walikuwa katika jeshi lako, watu wako wa vita; \q ngao na kofia ya chuma walizitundika ndani yako; \q wao walikupa fahari yako.
sw.B: Watu wa Uajemi, Ludi na Puti walikuwa askari katika jeshi lako. \q Walizitundika ngao zao na kofia zao za chuma ndani yako; \q walikupa fahari yako.
sw.R: Askari kutoka Uajemi, Ludi na Puti walitumika katika jeshi lako. \q Walitundika ngao zao na kofia zao za chuma ndani yako. \q Walikufanya uonekane wa fahari.

vi.L: Ba Tư, Lút và Phút ở trong quân đội ngươi, là những chiến binh của ngươi; \q khiên và mũ chiến chúng treo trong ngươi; \q chúng đã ban cho ngươi vẻ huy hoàng.
vi.B: Người Ba Tư, Lút và Phút phục vụ trong quân đội ngươi làm chiến binh của ngươi. \q Họ treo khiên và mũ chiến trong ngươi; \q họ làm cho ngươi thêm huy hoàng.
vi.R: Quân lính từ Ba Tư, Lút và Phút phục vụ trong quân đội của ngươi. \q Họ treo khiên và mũ chiến của mình bên trong ngươi. \q Họ làm cho ngươi trông thật huy hoàng.

decisions.choice: Persia, Lud and Put: hired soldiers from distant lands
decisions.reason: Tyre hired soldiers from far away. Put is Libya in north Africa (30:5; Jeremiah 46:9). Lud may be Lydia in Asia Minor or a people of Africa (Genesis 10:13; Isaiah 66:19). Persia was still a small land east of Babylon in Ezekiel's day; it is named again with Cush and Put in 38:5.

decisions.choice: shield and helmet hung in you: weapons on display
decisions.reason: Soldiers hung their shields on walls and towers as a show of strength (Song of Songs 4:4).

source.text: בְּנֵ֧י אַרְוַ֣ד וְחֵילֵ֗ךְ עַל־חוֹמוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב וְגַ֨מָּדִ֔ים בְּמִגְדְּלוֹתַ֖יִךְ הָי֑וּ שִׁלְטֵיהֶ֞ם תִּלּ֤וּ עַל־חוֹמוֹתַ֨יִךְ֙ סָבִ֔יב הֵ֖מָּה כָּלְל֥וּ יָפְיֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Arvad and Helech [were] on your walls all around, and Gammadites in your towers were; their shields they hung on your walls all around; they perfected your beauty.

en.L: The sons of Arvad and Helech [were] on your walls all around, \q and Gammadites were in your towers; \q their shields they hung on your walls all around; \q they made your beauty perfect.
en.B: Men of Arvad and Helech manned your walls on every side, \q and men of Gamad were in your towers. \q Their shields hung around your walls; \q they made your beauty perfect.
en.R: Soldiers from Arvad and Helech stood guard all around your walls. \q Men from Gamad were in your towers. \q They hung their shields all around your walls. \q They made you perfectly beautiful.

fr.L: Les fils d’Arvad et Hélek [étaient] sur tes murailles tout autour, \q et des Gammadiens étaient dans tes tours ; \q leurs boucliers, ils les suspendaient à tes murailles tout autour ; \q ils ont rendu parfaite ta beauté.
fr.B: Les hommes d’Arvad et de Hélek gardaient tes murailles tout autour, \q et les hommes de Gamad étaient dans tes tours. \q Leurs boucliers étaient suspendus tout autour de tes murailles ; \q ils ont rendu ta beauté parfaite.
fr.R: Des soldats d’Arvad et de Hélek montaient la garde tout autour de tes murailles. \q Des hommes de Gamad étaient dans tes tours. \q Ils accrochaient leurs boucliers tout autour de tes murailles. \q Ils t’ont rendue parfaitement belle.

es.L: Los hijos de Arvad y Helec [estaban] sobre tus muros alrededor, \q y los gamadeos estaban en tus torres; \q sus escudos colgaron sobre tus muros alrededor; \q ellos perfeccionaron tu hermosura.
es.B: Hombres de Arvad y de Helec vigilaban tus muros por todos lados, \q y hombres de Gamad estaban en tus torres. \q Sus escudos colgaban alrededor de tus muros; \q ellos hicieron perfecta tu hermosura.
es.R: Soldados de Arvad y de Helec hacían guardia alrededor de tus murallas. \q Hombres de Gamad estaban en tus torres. \q Colgaban sus escudos por todas tus murallas. \q Te hacían perfectamente hermosa.

sw.L: Wana wa Arvadi na Heleki [walikuwa] juu ya kuta zako pande zote, \q na Wagamadi walikuwa katika minara yako; \q ngao zao walizitundika juu ya kuta zako pande zote; \q wao waliukamilisha uzuri wako.
sw.B: Watu wa Arvadi na Heleki walilinda kuta zako pande zote, \q na watu wa Gamadi walikuwa katika minara yako. \q Ngao zao zilitundikwa kuzunguka kuta zako; \q waliukamilisha uzuri wako.
sw.R: Askari kutoka Arvadi na Heleki walilinda kuta zako pande zote. \q Watu kutoka Gamadi walikuwa katika minara yako. \q Walitundika ngao zao kuzunguka kuta zako. \q Walikufanya mzuri kabisa.

vi.L: Con cái A-vát và Hê-léc [ở] trên các tường thành ngươi chung quanh, \q và người Ga-mát ở trong các tháp của ngươi; \q khiên của chúng, chúng treo trên các tường thành ngươi chung quanh; \q chúng đã làm cho vẻ đẹp ngươi nên toàn hảo.
vi.B: Người A-vát và Hê-léc canh giữ khắp các tường thành ngươi, \q và người Ga-mát ở trong các tháp canh của ngươi. \q Khiên của họ treo khắp chung quanh tường thành ngươi; \q họ đã làm cho vẻ đẹp ngươi nên toàn hảo.
vi.R: Quân lính từ A-vát và Hê-léc đứng canh khắp chung quanh tường thành ngươi. \q Người Ga-mát ở trong các tháp canh của ngươi. \q Họ treo khiên của mình khắp chung quanh tường thành ngươi. \q Họ làm cho ngươi đẹp tuyệt vời.

decisions.choice: Helech: a place, or "your army"
decisions.reason: The word may be a place name, perhaps Cilicia in southern Asia Minor, or the word "your army" from verse 10.

decisions.choice: Gammadites: an unknown people
decisions.reason: The name occurs only here. Who they were is not known.

decisions.choice: they made your beauty perfect: the words of verse 4
decisions.reason: The description of the ship and its guard ends where it began.

decisions.choice: Men of Arvad (B); Soldiers from Arvad (R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the sons of Arvad"; the guards on the walls were soldiers, so Balanced and Readable say "men" and "soldiers".

decisions.choice: Arvad, Helec, los gamadeos (L) / Gamad (B, R)
decisions.reason: The little-known names are written as Spanish writes Hebrew names; Helech may be a place or 'your army', as the meaning decision says.

decisions.choice: "Hê-léc" and "người Ga-mát" as names at every level
decisions.reason: Transliterated as the English does; the meaning decisions give the other reading of Helech and say that the Gammadites are unknown.

source.text: תַּרְשִׁ֥ישׁ סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב כָּל־ה֑וֹן בְּכֶ֤סֶף בַּרְזֶל֙ בְּדִ֣יל וְעוֹפֶ֔רֶת נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Tarshish [was] your trader from [the] abundance of all wealth; for silver, iron, tin and lead they gave your wares.

en.L: Tarshish [was] your trader because of the abundance of all [kinds of] wealth; \q with silver, iron, tin and lead they paid for your wares.
en.B: Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of every kind; \q they traded silver, iron, tin and lead for your goods.
en.R: The people of Tarshish traded with you because you had so many good things to sell. \q They gave you silver, iron, tin and lead in exchange for your goods.

fr.L: Tarsis [était] ta marchande à cause de l’abondance de toute richesse ; \q avec de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb, ils payaient tes produits.
fr.B: Tarsis faisait commerce avec toi à cause de tes richesses de toute sorte ; \q on t’échangeait de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb contre tes produits.
fr.R: Les gens de Tarsis faisaient du commerce avec toi, parce que tu avais beaucoup de bonnes choses à vendre. \q Ils te donnaient de l’argent, du fer, de l’étain et du plomb en échange de tes produits.

es.L: Tarsis [era] tu comerciante por la abundancia de toda [clase de] riqueza; \q con plata, hierro, estaño y plomo pagaban tus productos.
es.B: Tarsis comerciaba contigo por tu gran riqueza de toda clase; \q a cambio de tus productos daban plata, hierro, estaño y plomo.
es.R: La gente de Tarsis comerciaba contigo porque tenías muchas cosas buenas que vender. \q Te daban plata, hierro, estaño y plomo a cambio de tus productos.

sw.L: Tarshishi [alikuwa] mfanyabiashara wako kwa sababu ya wingi wa mali za kila [aina]; \q kwa fedha, chuma, bati na risasi walilipia bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Tarshishi ilifanya biashara nawe kwa sababu ya utajiri wako mwingi wa kila aina; \q walibadilisha fedha, chuma, bati na risasi kwa bidhaa zako.
sw.R: Watu wa Tarshishi walifanya biashara nawe kwa sababu ulikuwa na vitu vingi vizuri vya kuuza. \q Walikupa fedha, chuma, bati na risasi kwa bidhaa zako.

vi.L: Ta-rê-si [là] kẻ buôn bán với ngươi vì sự dồi dào của mọi [thứ] của cải; \q chúng đã trả cho hàng hóa của ngươi bằng bạc, sắt, thiếc và chì.
vi.B: Ta-rê-si buôn bán với ngươi vì ngươi giàu có đủ mọi thứ; \q họ đem bạc, sắt, thiếc và chì đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Dân Ta-rê-si buôn bán với ngươi vì ngươi có rất nhiều hàng tốt để bán. \q Họ đưa cho ngươi bạc, sắt, thiếc và chì để đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: verses 12-24: Tyre's trading partners
decisions.reason: The list names Tyre's partners in trade and what each supplied, from the far west to Asia Minor, the north, Arabia and Mesopotamia. Several names and goods are rare or unknown, and decisions say where.

decisions.choice: Tarshish: a port in the far west
decisions.reason: Tarshish lay far to the west across the Mediterranean (Jonah 1:3). It is often placed in southern Spain, rich in metals.

decisions.choice: your wares: goods left in exchange
decisions.reason: The word for "wares" is found only in this chapter. It seems to mean goods given or left in exchange.

decisions.choice: the trading partners of 12-24 keep their published French names: "Tarsis", "Javan" (L, B; "la Grèce" at R), "Tubal", "Méshek", "Beth-Togarma", "Dedan", "Saba", "Raama", "Harân", "Assour"
decisions.reason: The term sheet's names table and the published Genesis 10 and 1 Chronicles 1.

decisions.choice: comerciante (L); comerciaba contigo (B, R)
decisions.reason: The trade list (12-24) keeps one wording through its verses: L keeps the noun 'comerciante' of the Hebrew, B and R use the verb, as the English does.

source.text: יָוָ֤ן תֻּבַל֙ וָמֶ֔שֶׁךְ הֵ֖מָּה רֹֽכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּנֶ֤פֶשׁ אָדָם֙ וּכְלֵ֣י נְחֹ֔שֶׁת נָתְנ֖וּ מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Javan, Tubal and Meshech, they [were] your traders; for [the] lives of humans and vessels of bronze they gave your merchandise.

en.L: Javan, Tubal and Meshech, they [were] your traders; \q with the lives of human beings and vessels of bronze they paid for your merchandise.
en.B: Javan, Tubal and Meshech traded with you; \q they exchanged slaves and bronze vessels for your goods.
en.R: The people of Greece, Tubal and Meshech traded with you. \q They sold you slaves and things made of bronze in exchange for your goods.

fr.L: Javan, Tubal et Méshek, eux [étaient] tes marchands ; \q avec des vies humaines et des objets de bronze ils payaient tes marchandises.
fr.B: Javan, Tubal et Méshek faisaient commerce avec toi ; \q ils échangeaient des esclaves et des objets de bronze contre tes marchandises.
fr.R: Les gens de la Grèce, de Tubal et de Méshek faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Ils te vendaient des esclaves et des objets en bronze en échange de tes marchandises.

es.L: Javán, Tubal y Mesec, ellos [eran] tus comerciantes; \q con vidas humanas y utensilios de bronce pagaban tus mercancías.
es.B: Javán, Tubal y Mesec comerciaban contigo; \q a cambio de tus mercancías daban esclavos y utensilios de bronce.
es.R: La gente de Grecia, de Tubal y de Mesec comerciaba contigo. \q Te vendían esclavos y objetos de bronce a cambio de tus mercancías.

sw.L: Yavani, Tubali na Mesheki, wao [walikuwa] wafanyabiashara wako; \q kwa nafsi za wanadamu na vyombo vya shaba walilipia bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Yavani, Tubali na Mesheki walifanya biashara nawe; \q walibadilisha watumwa na vyombo vya shaba kwa bidhaa zako.
sw.R: Watu wa Ugiriki, Tubali na Mesheki walifanya biashara nawe. \q Walikuuzia watumwa na vitu vya shaba kwa bidhaa zako.

vi.L: Gia-van, Tu-banh và Mê-siếc, chúng [là] những kẻ buôn bán với ngươi; \q chúng đã trả cho hàng hóa của ngươi bằng mạng người và đồ đồng.
vi.B: Gia-van, Tu-banh và Mê-siếc buôn bán với ngươi; \q họ đem nô lệ và đồ đồng đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Dân Hy Lạp, Tu-banh và Mê-siếc buôn bán với ngươi. \q Họ bán cho ngươi nô lệ và đồ đồng để đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: Javan, Tubal and Meshech: the Greeks and peoples of Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Javan is Ionia, the Greeks of the Aegean coasts and islands (Genesis 10:2; Daniel 8:21). Tubal and Meshech were peoples of central and eastern Asia Minor (32:26; 38:2).

decisions.choice: the lives of human beings: slaves
decisions.reason: People were bought and sold. Joel 4:6 accuses Tyre and Sidon of selling the people of Judah to the Greeks, and Amos 1:9 condemns Tyre's slave trade.

decisions.choice: slaves (B, R)
decisions.reason: Literal keeps "the lives of human beings". Balanced and Readable say "slaves", since people sold as property are meant, under the style guide's rule for slavery.

decisions.choice: Greece
decisions.reason: Readable says "Greece" for Javan here, as the name is used in Daniel 8:21.

decisions.choice: "Yavani" (L, B); "Ugiriki" (R)
decisions.reason: Following the English levels, as the term sheet says; "mtumwa" for the slaves at B and R, since slavery itself is meant.

decisions.choice: "Gia-van" (L, B) / "Hy Lạp" (R); "Tu-banh", "Mê-siếc"; "mạng người" (L) / "nô lệ" (B, R)
decisions.reason: The names as Genesis 10:2. The trading partners are "họ" at B and R, "chúng" at L for the bare Hebrew "they"; the same pattern runs through verses 12-24.

source.text: מִבֵּ֖ית תּוֹגַרְמָ֑ה סוּסִ֤ים וּפָֽרָשִׁים֙ וּפְרָדִ֔ים נָתְנ֖וּ עִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: From [the] house of Togarmah, horses and steeds and mules they gave [for] your wares.

en.L: From Beth-togarmah, \q horses and steeds and mules they gave for your wares.
en.B: From Beth-togarmah \q they traded horses, war horses and mules for your goods.
en.R: People from Beth-togarmah \q traded horses, war horses and mules for your goods.

fr.L: De Beth-Togarma, \q des chevaux, des coursiers et des mulets, ils [les] donnaient pour tes produits.
fr.B: De Beth-Togarma, \q on t’échangeait des chevaux, des chevaux de guerre et des mulets contre tes produits.
fr.R: Des gens de Beth-Togarma \q t’échangeaient des chevaux, des chevaux de guerre et des mulets contre tes produits.

es.L: De Bet-togarma, \q caballos y corceles y mulos daban por tus productos.
es.B: Desde Bet-togarma \q te daban caballos, caballos de guerra y mulos por tus productos.
es.R: La gente de Bet-togarma \q te daba caballos, caballos de guerra y mulos por tus productos.

sw.L: Kutoka Beth-togarma, \q farasi na farasi wa vita na nyumbu walitoa kwa bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Kutoka Beth-togarma \q walibadilisha farasi, farasi wa vita na nyumbu kwa bidhaa zako.
sw.R: Watu kutoka Beth-togarma \q walibadilisha farasi, farasi wa vita na nyumbu kwa bidhaa zako.

vi.L: Từ Bết-Tô-ga-ma, \q chúng đã đem ngựa, ngựa chiến và la đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.B: Từ Bết-Tô-ga-ma, \q họ đem ngựa, ngựa chiến và la đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Người từ Bết-Tô-ga-ma \q đem ngựa, ngựa chiến và la đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: Beth-togarmah: a land of horses in eastern Asia Minor
decisions.reason: Togarmah is a son of Gomer (Genesis 10:3) and is placed in the far north (38:6), perhaps in the region of Armenia.

decisions.choice: steeds: riding or war horses
decisions.reason: The word usually means horsemen, but beside "horses" and "mules" it means horses for riding or for war.

source.text: בְּנֵ֤י דְדָן֙ רֹֽכְלַ֔יִךְ אִיִּ֥ים רַבִּ֖ים סְחֹרַ֣ת יָדֵ֑ךְ קַרְנ֥וֹת שֵׁן֙ וְהָבְנִ֔ים הֵשִׁ֖יבוּ אֶשְׁכָּרֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: [The] sons of Dedan [were] your traders; many coastlands [were the] market of your hand; horns of ivory and ebony they brought back [as] your payment.

en.L: The sons of Dedan [were] your traders; \q many coastlands [were] the market of your hand; \q horns of ivory and ebony they brought back [as] your payment.
en.B: The people of Dedan traded with you; \q many coastlands were markets under your control; \q they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony.
en.R: The people of Dedan traded with you. \q Many lands across the sea bought your goods. \q They paid you with elephant tusks and ebony wood.

fr.L: Les fils de Dedan [étaient] tes marchands ; \q des îles nombreuses [étaient] le marché de ta main ; \q des cornes d’ivoire et de l’ébène, ils te [les] rapportaient [en] paiement.
fr.B: Les gens de Dedan faisaient commerce avec toi ; \q des îles nombreuses étaient des marchés sous ton contrôle ; \q elles te payaient en défenses d’ivoire et en ébène.
fr.R: Les gens de Dedan faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Beaucoup de pays au-delà de la mer achetaient tes marchandises. \q Ils te payaient avec des défenses d’éléphant et du bois d’ébène.

es.L: Los hijos de Dedán [eran] tus comerciantes; \q muchas costas [eran] el mercado de tu mano; \q colmillos de marfil y ébano te traían [como] pago.
es.B: La gente de Dedán comerciaba contigo; \q muchas costas lejanas eran mercados bajo tu control; \q te pagaban con colmillos de marfil y ébano.
es.R: La gente de Dedán comerciaba contigo. \q Muchas tierras al otro lado del mar compraban tus productos. \q Te pagaban con colmillos de elefante y madera de ébano.

sw.L: Wana wa Dedani [walikuwa] wafanyabiashara wako; \q visiwa vingi [vilikuwa] soko la mkono wako; \q pembe za ndovu na mpingo walikuletea [kama] malipo yako.
sw.B: Watu wa Dedani walifanya biashara nawe; \q pwani nyingi za mbali zilikuwa masoko chini ya mamlaka yako; \q walikulipa kwa pembe za ndovu na mpingo.
sw.R: Watu wa Dedani walifanya biashara nawe. \q Nchi nyingi ng'ambo ya bahari zilinunua bidhaa zako. \q Walikulipa kwa pembe za tembo na mbao za mpingo.

vi.L: Con cái Đê-đan [là] những kẻ buôn bán với ngươi; \q nhiều hải đảo [là] thị trường trong tay ngươi; \q chúng đem ngà voi và gỗ mun về [làm] tiền trả cho ngươi.
vi.B: Dân Đê-đan buôn bán với ngươi; \q nhiều hải đảo là thị trường dưới quyền ngươi; \q họ trả cho ngươi bằng ngà voi và gỗ mun.
vi.R: Dân Đê-đan buôn bán với ngươi. \q Nhiều miền xa bên kia biển mua hàng của ngươi. \q Họ trả cho ngươi bằng ngà voi và gỗ mun.

decisions.choice: the sons of Dedan
decisions.reason: Dedan, an Arabian people, comes again in verse 20. The Greek translation reads "Rhodes" here (stated from general knowledge); the Hebrew letters for d and r look much alike, and Rhodes would fit the "coastlands" that follow. The Hebrew is kept.

decisions.choice: the market of your hand: markets under your control
decisions.reason: The phrase seems to mean that many coastlands traded at Tyre's direction, as its agents or customers.

decisions.choice: horns of ivory and ebony: luxuries from far away
decisions.reason: Elephant tusks and black ebony wood came from Africa or India by long trade routes.

source.text: אֲרָ֥ם סֹחַרְתֵּ֖ךְ מֵרֹ֣ב מַעֲשָׂ֑יִךְ בְּ֠נֹפֶךְ אַרְגָּמָ֨ן וְרִקְמָ֤ה וּבוּץ֙ וְרָאמֹ֣ת וְכַדְכֹּ֔ד נָתְנ֖וּ בְּעִזְבוֹנָֽיִךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Aram [was] your trader from [the] abundance of your works; for turquoise, purple, and embroidery, and fine linen, and coral, and rubies they gave your wares.

en.L: Aram [was] your trader because of the abundance of your products; \q with turquoise, purple and embroidered work, and fine linen and coral and rubies they paid for your wares.
en.B: Aram did business with you because you had so many products; \q they gave turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered work, fine linen, coral and rubies for your goods.
en.R: The people of Aram traded with you because you made so many things. \q They gave you turquoise, purple cloth, embroidered cloth, fine linen, coral and rubies for your goods.

fr.L: Aram [était] ta marchande à cause de l’abondance de tes ouvrages ; \q avec des turquoises, de la pourpre et des broderies, et du fin lin, et du corail, et des rubis, ils payaient tes produits.
fr.B: Aram faisait commerce avec toi à cause de tes nombreux ouvrages ; \q on te donnait des turquoises, des étoffes pourpres, des broderies, du fin lin, du corail et des rubis contre tes produits.
fr.R: Les gens d’Aram faisaient du commerce avec toi, parce que tu fabriquais beaucoup de choses. \q Ils te donnaient des turquoises, du tissu pourpre, des broderies, du fin lin, du corail et des rubis en échange de tes produits.

es.L: Aram [era] tu comerciante por la abundancia de tus productos; \q con turquesa, púrpura y bordados, y lino fino y coral y rubíes pagaban tus mercancías.
es.B: Aram comerciaba contigo porque tenías muchos productos; \q a cambio de tus mercancías daban turquesa, tela de púrpura, bordados, lino fino, coral y rubíes.
es.R: La gente de Aram comerciaba contigo porque hacías muchas cosas. \q Te daban turquesa, tela de púrpura, tela bordada, lino fino, coral y rubíes a cambio de tus productos.

sw.L: Aramu [alikuwa] mfanyabiashara wako kwa sababu ya wingi wa kazi zako; \q kwa feruzi, zambarau na kazi ya kutariziwa, na kitani safi, na marijani na yakuti nyekundu walilipia bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Aramu ilifanya biashara nawe kwa sababu ulikuwa na bidhaa nyingi; \q walitoa feruzi, nguo ya zambarau, kazi ya kutariziwa, kitani safi, marijani na yakuti nyekundu kwa bidhaa zako.
sw.R: Watu wa Aramu walifanya biashara nawe kwa sababu ulitengeneza vitu vingi. \q Walikupa feruzi, nguo ya zambarau, nguo zilizotariziwa, kitani safi, marijani na yakuti nyekundu kwa bidhaa zako.

vi.L: A-ram [là] kẻ buôn bán với ngươi vì sự dồi dào của các sản phẩm ngươi; \q chúng đã trả cho hàng hóa của ngươi bằng ngọc lam, vải tím, đồ thêu, vải gai mịn, san hô và hồng ngọc.
vi.B: A-ram buôn bán với ngươi vì ngươi có rất nhiều sản phẩm; \q họ đem ngọc lam, vải tím, đồ thêu, vải gai mịn, san hô và hồng ngọc đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Dân A-ram buôn bán với ngươi vì ngươi làm ra rất nhiều thứ. \q Họ đưa cho ngươi ngọc lam, vải tím, vải thêu, vải gai mịn, san hô và hồng ngọc để đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: Aram
decisions.reason: Many Hebrew manuscripts read "Edom", which differs from "Aram" by one similar letter (stated from general knowledge). Edom would fit the gems, and Aram's chief city, Damascus, is named separately in verse 18. The standard text is kept.

decisions.choice: turquoise, coral and rubies: precious stones whose names are uncertain
decisions.reason: The names of gems in Hebrew are hard to identify. The first may be turquoise or emerald (28:13; Exodus 28:18), the second coral (Job 28:18), the third ruby or agate (Isaiah 54:12).

decisions.choice: "feruzi", "marijani", "yakuti nyekundu" for turquoise, coral and rubies
decisions.reason: "feruzi" as the Swahili Exodus 28:18; the identifications are uncertain, as the meaning decision says.

source.text: יְהוּדָה֙ וְאֶ֣רֶץ יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל הֵ֖מָּה רֹכְלָ֑יִךְ בְּחִטֵּ֣י מִ֠נִּית וּפַנַּ֨ג וּדְבַ֤שׁ וָשֶׁ֨מֶן֙ וָצֹ֔רִי נָתְנ֖וּ מַעֲרָבֵֽךְ׃

records.literal_gloss: Judah and [the] land of Israel, they [were] your traders; with wheat of Minnith and pannag and honey and oil and balm they gave your merchandise.

en.L: Judah and the land of Israel, they [were] your traders; \q with wheat of Minnith and pannag and honey and oil and balm they paid for your merchandise.
en.B: Judah and the land of Israel were your traders; \q for your goods they gave wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, oil and balm.
en.R: The people of Judah and Israel traded with you. \q They gave you wheat from Minnith, millet, honey, olive oil and balm for your goods.

fr.L: Juda et le pays d’Israël, eux [étaient] tes marchands ; \q avec du blé de Minnith, et du pannag, et du miel, et de l’huile, et du baume, ils payaient tes marchandises.
fr.B: Juda et le pays d’Israël faisaient commerce avec toi ; \q ils te donnaient pour tes marchandises du blé de Minnith, du millet, du miel, de l’huile et du baume.
fr.R: Les gens de Juda et d’Israël faisaient du commerce avec toi. \q Ils te donnaient du blé de Minnith, du millet, du miel, de l’huile d’olive et du baume en échange de tes marchandises.

es.L: Judá y la tierra de Israel, ellos [eran] tus comerciantes; \q con trigo de Minit y pannag y miel y aceite y bálsamo pagaban tus mercancías.
es.B: Judá y la tierra de Israel comerciaban contigo; \q a cambio de tus mercancías daban trigo de Minit, mijo, miel, aceite y bálsamo.
es.R: La gente de Judá y de Israel comerciaba contigo. \q Te daban trigo de Minit, mijo, miel, aceite de oliva y bálsamo a cambio de tus mercancías.

sw.L: Yuda na nchi ya Israeli, wao [walikuwa] wafanyabiashara wako; \q kwa ngano ya Minithi na panagi na asali na mafuta na zeri walilipia bidhaa zako.
sw.B: Yuda na nchi ya Israeli walifanya biashara nawe; \q kwa bidhaa zako walitoa ngano ya Minithi, mtama, asali, mafuta na zeri.
sw.R: Watu wa Yuda na Israeli walifanya biashara nawe. \q Walikupa ngano ya Minithi, mtama, asali, mafuta ya zeituni na zeri kwa bidhaa zako.

vi.L: Giu-đa và đất Y-sơ-ra-ên, họ [là] những kẻ buôn bán với ngươi; \q họ đã trả cho hàng hóa của ngươi bằng lúa mì Min-nít, pa-nác, mật ong, dầu và nhũ hương.
vi.B: Giu-đa và đất Y-sơ-ra-ên buôn bán với ngươi; \q họ đem lúa mì Min-nít, hạt kê, mật ong, dầu và nhũ hương đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.
vi.R: Dân Giu-đa và Y-sơ-ra-ên buôn bán với ngươi. \q Họ đưa cho ngươi lúa mì Min-nít, hạt kê, mật ong, dầu ô-liu và nhũ hương để đổi lấy hàng hóa của ngươi.

decisions.choice: Judah and the land of Israel among Tyre's partners
decisions.reason: Israel had long supplied Tyre with farm produce in exchange for timber and skill (1 Kings 5:25; Acts 12:20). God's people too were part of Tyre's world of trade.

decisions.choice: Minnith: a town east of the Jordan
decisions.reason: Minnith is named in Judges 11:33, in the land of Ammon. The wheat may have come from there or been named for it.

decisions.choice: pannag: an unknown food
decisions.reason: The word occurs only here. It may be a kind of millet, a pastry, or some other foodstuff. Literal keeps the Hebrew word.

decisions.choice: balm: a healing resin
decisions.reason: Balm was a famous product of Gilead (Genesis 37:25; Jeremiah 8:22).

decisions.choice: millet (B, R); pannag (L)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable give a likely sense of the unknown word (m3); Readable says "olive oil" for "oil".

decisions.choice: "pannag" (L), "millet" (B, R), as the English
decisions.reason: The word is unknown (footnoted in the meaning decision); French follows the English levels until the founder rules on the open question.

decisions.choice: pannag (L); mijo (B, R)
decisions.reason: Nobody knows what 'pannag' was; L keeps the Hebrew word, B and R follow the English guess 'millet'. Minit keeps the published spelling (Judges 11:33).

decisions.choice: "panagi" (L); "mtama" (B, R) for pannag
decisions.reason: Literal transliterates the unknown word; Balanced and Readable give millet as the English does. "zeri" for balm, as the Swahili Genesis 37:25.
